bcb35e44c3a7505507ed369832a577d874faebed.summary: This is an archived U.S. Department of Justice video landing page, dated 2022-04-06. Its title says the Attorney General announced enforcement actions to disrupt and prosecute Russian criminal activity. The captured text holds only navigation, the title, the date and topic labels (Cybercrime, Countering Nation-State Threats). It describes no actors, tools, techniques, victims or figures, so it is not treated as a threat report and no facts are recorded.
hedges: This is archived content from the U.S. Department of Justice website. The information here may be outdated and links may no longer function.

bc0570ada4139628d9ed0a72585bf067f5408abb.summary: The report says cosmetics maker Estée Lauder confirmed a cyberattack in which hackers gained unauthorized access, shut some systems, and stole some data. Ransomware groups Clop and ALPHV (also known as BlackCat) listed the company as a victim. BlackCat claims to have stolen more than 130 GB without encrypting the network. Clop may have exploited vulnerabilities in MOVEit file transfer software. The nature and scope of the attack were yet to be determined.

bc874da8af8876fcb047be42c580cdc649e4e1ee.summary: An academic study by Delft University of Technology and an independent researcher, analysing ransom payments tracked via the crowdsourced Ransomwhere tool. It records 13,497 payments to 87 criminal actors, worth over $101 million in Bitcoin. It contrasts two markets: commodity ransomware and Ransomware as a Service (RaaS), which became widespread after 2019 and earns more per address. RaaS actors typically use a new address per payment, launder funds quickly, and favour mixers and fraudulent exchanges. Commodity actors make many smaller cash-outs. The report says its dataset is incomplete…
